ION updated the Project Management Plan as the project progressed. 4.1.2 Technology Maturation Plan ION developed a TMP that described the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of the ICE-31® technology, related the proposed project work to the maturation of the proposed technology, and described the expected TRL at the end of the project. It also described future post-project research and development necessary to further mature the technology. Both an Initial TMP and a Final TMP were completed as part of the project. 4.1.3 Environmental Health & Safety Risk Assessment ION, with support from Hellman, an EH&S firm, completed the Initial EH&S Risk Assessment. A Final EH&S Risk Assessment has been submitted. 4.1.4 Techno-Economic Analysis ION completed a Preliminary and Final Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA). 4.2 Design of NGCC 1 MWe (10 tpd) Engineering Scale System (BP1) ION led the project team through the determination and evaluation of the design requirements for installing a carbon capture system at the NGCC host site. Furthermore, ION oversaw the design of the 1 MWe (10 tpd) engineering scale system using an established systems-engineering approach, which led to a completed Design Package with firm costs for proceeding to the construction phase. ION Clean Energy 8 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 4.2.1 Carbon Capture System Basic Engineering ION generated documents required to plan the building of the Carbon Capture Island. These documents included Process Flow Diagrams, Heat and Mass Balances, utility needs, equipment lists, Process and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), General Arrangement/3D models, and a refined set of requirements, supported by performance models and system analyses. These documents produced well-defined requirements, specific to the Carbon Capture Island, that formed the basis of inspection and acceptance criteria. This subtask included a HAZOP performed by all stakeholders and the development of the Process Design Package and the Fixed Price Proposal. 4.2.2 Balance of Plant Design ION completed the design work for the BOP activities that were necessary to facilitate the location and operation of the CCS at the generating station, which resulted in a construction cost estimate for BOP. This task included design for site work (containment and foundations), flue gas tie-in, cooling water system, steam and condensate system, electrical supply system, and pipe racks. 4.2.3 Host Site Agreement and Permitting ION worked with the host site organization to develop and sign a Host Site Agreement for the campaign. Additionally, all required permits, including the California Building Office (CBO), Bay Area Air Quality Management District (BAAQMD), and the Delta Diablo Sanitation District (DDSD) for the engineering scale demonstration, were developed and submitted to the appropriate regulatory authorities. The engineering scale project required cooperation with the lead permitting authority for all power plants 50 MW or greater. 4.3 Construction of NGCC 1 MWe (10 tpd) Engineering Scale System (BP2) ION supervised the construction of the engineering scale system by the CCS vendor (KMPS) as well as the BOP systems by the BOP engineering firm, S&L.
